To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the association between the divorce of a mother and child externalizing behavior problems was partially mediated by maternal depressive/withdrawn behavior when the child was in the fourth and the fifth grades.
the association between parental divorce and child adjustment problems is partially mediated by depressive and withdrawn parenting.

(a) depressive/withdrawn parental behaviors mediate the association between divorce, and child adjustment at school and home, and (b) the association between divorce (or depressive/withdrawn maternal behavior) and child externalizing problems is stronger in the early elementary school years than it is in the later elementary school years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how divorce affects children.
the role of depressive parenting in mediating the association between divorce status and child adjustment problems.
the impact of divorce on children's behavior problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
depressive/withdrawn mothering mediates the linkages between divorce and child adjustment problems.

divorce, depressive/ withdrawn parenting, and children's externalizing behavior are all associated with each other and that the association between the first and third is partially mediated by the second.
depressive/withdrawn mothering is a significant factor in children's adjustment to divorce and that it is associated with children's externalizing and internalising behavior at home and school.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the association between family disruption and child adjustment problems is partially mediated by depressive parenting. (Author abstract)
divorce and single motherhood are associated with increased depressive/withdrawn behaviors on the part of mothers and that these behaviors in turn have an impact on child adjustment.
the effects of divorce are more complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
depressive/withdrawn mothering is a significant mediator between divorce and children's adjustment.
the association between family structure and child adjustment may be explained, at least in part, by parenting behavior.
the association between parental divorce and child adjustment problems was partially mediated by the mother's depressive/withdrawn behavior.
